people.name: Lee de Forest
people.extract:
Lee de Forest was an American inventor, electrical engineer, and early pioneer in electronics of fundamental importance. He invented the first practical electronic amplifier,
the three-element "Audion" triode vacuum tube in 1908. This helped start the Electronic Age, and enabled the development of the electronic oscillator. These made radio broadcasting and long-distance telephone lines possible, and led to the development of talking motion pictures, among countless other applications.
highlights: Invented the "Audion" triode vacuum tube in 1908.
Pioneered electronics, enabling radio broadcasting and long-distance telephony.
His inventions led to talking motion pictures.

people.name: Hellmuth Walter
people.extract: Hellmuth Walter was a German engineer who pioneered research into rocket engines and gas turbines. His most noteworthy contributions were rocket motors for the Messerschmitt Me 163 and Bachem Ba 349 interceptor aircraft, so-called Starthilfe jettisonable rocket propulsion units used for a variety of Luftwaffe aircraft during World War II, and a revolutionary new propulsion system for submarines known as air-independent propulsion (AIP).
highlights: Pioneered research into rocket engines and gas turbines.
Developed rocket motors for Me 163 and Ba 349 aircraft.

people.name: James Franck
people.extract: James Franck was a German–American physicist who shared the 1925 Nobel Prize in Physics with Gustav Hertz "for their discovery of the laws governing the impact of an electron upon an atom."
highlights: Shared 1925 Nobel Prize in Physics with Gustav Hertz.
Awarded for electron impact upon atom discovery.
